title: anthropics/skills — Public repository for Agent Skills
content:
Note: This repository contains Anthropic's implementation of skills for Claude. For information about the Agent Skills standard, see agentskills.io.
Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.
For more information, check out:
- What are skills?
- Using skills in Claude
- How to create custom skills
- Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. These skills range from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows (communications, branding, etc.).
Each skill is self-contained in its own folder with a SKILL.md file containing the instructions and metadata that Claude uses. Browse through these skills to get inspiration for your own skills or to understand different patterns and approaches.
Many skills in this repo are open source (Apache 2.0). We've also included the document creation & editing skills that power Claude's document capabilities under the hood in the skills/docx, skills/pdf, skills/pptx, and skills/xlsx subfolders. These are source-available, not open source, but we wanted to share these with developers as a reference for more complex skills that are actively used in a production AI application.
These skills are provided for demonstration and educational purposes only. While some of these capabilities may be available in Claude, the implementations and behaviors you receive from Claude may differ from what is shown in these skills. These skills are meant to illustrate patterns and possibilities. Always test skills thoroughly in your own environment before relying on them for critical tasks.
- ./skills: Skill examples for Creative & Design, Development & Technical, Enterprise & Communication, and Document Skills
- ./spec: The Agent Skills specification
- ./template: Skill template
You can register this repository as a Claude Code Plugin marketplace by running the following command in Claude Code:
/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
Then, to install a specific set of skills:
- Select Browse and install plugins
- Select anthropic-agent-skills
- Select document-skills orexample-skills
- Select Install now
Alternatively, directly install either Plugin via:
/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
After installing the plugin, you can use the skill by just mentioning it. For instance, if you install the document-skills plugin from the marketplace, you can ask Claude Code to do something like: "Use the PDF skill to extract the form fields from path/to/some-file.pdf"
These example skills are all already available to paid plans in Claude.ai.
To use any skill from this repository or upload custom skills, follow the instructions in Using skills in Claude.
You can use Anthropic's pre-built skills, and upload custom skills, via the Claude API. See the Skills API Quickstart for more.
Skills are simple to create - just a folder with a SKILL.md file containing YAML frontmatter and instructions. You can use the template-skill in this repository as a starting point:
---
name: my-skill-name
description: A clear description of what this skill does and when to use it
---
# My Skill Name
[Add your instructions here that Claude will follow when this skill is active]
## Examples
- Example usage 1
- Example usage 2
## Guidelines
- Guideline 1
- Guideline 2
The frontmatter requires only two fields:
- name - A unique identifier for your skill (lowercase, hyphens for spaces)
- description - A complete description of what the skill does and when to use it
The markdown content below contains the instructions, examples, and guidelines that Claude will follow. For more details, see How to create custom skills.
Skills are a great way to teach Claude how to get better at using specific pieces of software. As we see awesome example skills from partners, we may highlight some of them here:
- Notion - Notion Skills for Claude

report.summary: Anthropic open-sources example Agent Skills, defining a portable standard packaged as folders with SKILL.md for Claude and other agents.
report.background: Anthropic's skills repository formalizes a pattern the company has been developing for making AI agents more capable at specialized tasks. Rather than relying on the model to improvise every time, skills are packaged bundles of instructions, scripts, and resources loaded dynamically to execute a task in a repeatable way. The repo includes examples spanning creative work, development tools, enterprise communication, and document generation. A notable detail is that Anthropic is sharing source-available versions of the document skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx) that power Claude's production document features, while the examples themselves are under Apache 2.0. By publishing the specification alongside working reference skills, Anthropic is positioning skills as an interoperability layer for agent capabilities, not just a Claude-specific feature. This resembles the approach with MCP, where Anthropic released a spec and established a standard across vendors. The repository's plugin marketplace integration with Claude Code hints that Anthropic expects third-party developers and companies to distribute skills exactly as code plugins are distributed today.
key_points: Skills are simple bundles of instructions, scripts, and resources stored in folders with a SKILL.md metadata file. The format requires only a name and description in YAML frontmatter plus markdown instructions, making it easy for developers to create custom capabilities for Claude or other compatible agents.

The repository features examples across creative, technical, and enterprise domains, plus the source-available docx, pdf, pptx, and xlsx skills behind Claude's real document features. These production-grade examples give developers a reference for building complex skills beyond simple prompt instructions.

Anthropic has published the Agent Skills specification in the repo and links to agentskills.io, signaling a push to standardize how agent capabilities are shared. The effort parallels Anthropic's MCP strategy and invites other agent frameworks to adopt the same format.

Claude Code users can register this repository as a plugin marketplace and install skills directly. For example, installing the document-skills plugin allows users to invoke a PDF skill with natural language commands, lowering the barrier between discovering a skill and actively using it.

The examples are for demonstration and education; they don't guarantee identical behavior in production Claude. Anthropic cautions developers to test skills in their own environments, especially since document skills are source-available rather than fully open source.
report.impact: This release accelerates the shift from monolithic AI assistants to composable, purpose-built agent behaviors. Standardizing skills as folders with SKILL.md makes capabilities portable, shareable, and independent of a single vendor's internal implementation—similar to how browser extensions normalized customization. Developers can build workflows that combine Anthropic's document generation, analysis, and enterprise skills with custom automations, potentially reusing the same skills across different agent frameworks if the spec gains traction. Regular users benefit indirectly through richer applications: document creation infused with brand guidelines, faster data reports, and more reliable agent execution based on example patterns. For the industry, Anthropic's decision to publish both the specification and reference implementations lowers barriers to entry, but also raises questions about whether skills, like MCP, will become the dominant standard versus other emergent agent tooling. Ultimately it suggests agents will be defined less by base model capabilities and more by the ecosystem of skills attached to them.
report.tools: Developers and curious users should watch the agentskills.io standard site, the anthropics/skills repo itself, and Anthropic's Skills API Quickstart. Claude Code users can add the repository as a plugin marketplace with /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills, then install document-skills or example-skills. Those building their own capabilities can start from the included template-skill folder or adapt the open-source examples to explore efficient SKILL.md authoring patterns.
